<SUMMARY>The period saw escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia, with President Trump blaming Iran for downing a US Apache helicopter and vowing retaliation, alongside continued Israeli military actions in Lebanon. This conflict contributed to a global energy shock, causing China's wholesale inflation to hit a near four-year high and US inflation to jump to 4.2% in May, while Germany faces recession risks. Concurrently, the global AI and semiconductor sectors experienced volatility, with Taiwan proposing stricter export controls on AI chips to China, aligning with US efforts to manage technological outflows. The US stock market initially plunged due to AI hardware sell-offs but later rebounded amidst easing geopolitical tensions and renewed AI optimism. Efforts to strengthen critical mineral supply chains and semiconductor manufacturing capacity were also prominent, particularly in the US and Africa.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>Escalating US-Iran military tensions following the downing of a US Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz present a critical red flag for regional stability and global energy security, with Iran threatening to target regional energy infrastructure. Taiwan's consideration of a criminal ban on AI chip exports to all customers in China indicates a significant tightening of technological restrictions, potentially exacerbating US-China tech rivalry. The impact of the Middle East conflict on global supply chains for critical materials like aluminum, evidenced by the Diet Coke can shortage in India, highlights broader economic vulnerabilities.</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:**
Taiwan is tightening export controls on AI chip sales to China, aligning its regulations with the United States. This strategic maneuver aims to block the export of cutting-edge technologies, including AI servers powered by Nvidia chips, from Taiwan to China. Taiwan is considering a criminal ban on AI chip exports to all customers in China, which would make smuggling servers a crime. Chinese military jets circled Taiwan as AI supply chain chiefs gathered at Computex. Jupiter Asset Management’s Sam Konrad was forced to sell TSMC, Samsung, and MediaTek shares amid an AI stock rally, highlighting market concentration risks. AMD and Nvidia Taiwan investment plans are tightening AI supply chain competition. An AI shift to inference is opening new supply-chain opportunities for InWin and Y.S. Tech. Polymatech established an Asia-Pacific Advanced Manufacturing Hub in Singapore.

**Americas:**
Production AI is pushing private cloud back into the center of enterprise infrastructure, with Broadcom Inc.’s VMware making the private cloud case for AI. Arista’s 1.6T announcement is an Ethernet inflection point for the networking industry, supporting the AI supersystem shift. Crusoe announced it has contracted 4.9 gigawatts of AI infrastructure spanning its data center projects and capacity for Crusoe Cloud. Anthropic opened the most powerful version of its Claude artificial intelligence model to the general public, restricting its use in sensitive areas. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 2.17%, losing over 560 points, as AI and semiconductor stocks extended their sell-off, with Super Micro Computer shares down 11% and Dell Technologies sliding 9%. Texas Instruments is a pillar of America’s chip comeback in Utah’s Silicon Slopes. UT Austin was selected to help lead a national expansion of the semiconductor workforce, connecting employers, educators, and workforce partners across America's semiconductor-dense region. Spirit Electronics announced managed access to U.S.-based resources. D-Matrix, a Microsoft-backed company, is entering full production of an AI chip that it claims is 10 times faster than a GPU and bypasses memory shortages. Musk's Terafab targets 1TW chip output to double US production.

**Europe:**
Google secured Intel to manufacture more than 3 million AI chips for 2028 production. Nvidia is testing Intel’s 18A process and advanced packaging for future GPU architectures. The UK plans to buy AI chips from British tech firms.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Asia:**
A Chinese start-up announced its nanoimprint technology can produce optical chips without DUV, potentially offering a solution for the Chinese semiconductor industry unable to import ASML equipment.

**Americas:**
EUV lithography machines are at the epicenter of the AI computing shortage crisis, even as ASML Holding reached a new high, yet its valuation remains discounted by the market.

**Europe:**
The ASML chief warned the EU against directing chip supplies.
</LITHO>
<REE>
**Americas:**
A former Pentagon and CIA advisor states the U.S. is dangerously dependent on foreign supply chains for metals available under American soil, predicting that President Trump will change this by June 30. Apple-sized rocks four kilometers below the central Pacific Ocean, in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone between Mexico and Hawaii, contain more cobalt and manganese than all known land deposits combined, with mining companies racing to extract them. Pomerantz LLP is investigating claims on behalf of investors of Sigma Lithium Corporation.

**Africa:**
New Frontier Minerals Limited announced it is commencing characterization and metallurgical studies at the Pomme Rare Earths Elements Project, located approximately 50 km northwest of Mon. The global Electrolytic Manganese Dioxide (EMD) market, valued at US$ 945 million in 2025, is anticipated to reach US$ 1452 million by 2032. Critical minerals are catalyzing a second scramble for Africa, and the region seeks to benefit beyond just refining.

**Oceania:**
Ampera, a Florida-based nuclear energy startup, established Ampera Australia Pty Ltd in February 2026 to secure thorium supply from an Australian mine for its advanced reactor programme.
</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:**
Taiwan is tightening export controls on AI chip sales to China, aligning its regulations with the United States. Taiwan is considering far stricter export controls that would restrict AI chip sales to every customer in China, making smuggling servers a crime. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declined Senate testimony on AI, China, and exports. China’s May wholesale inflation hit a near four-year high on Iran war-led higher input costs and the AI boom.

**Europe:**
ASML chief warned the EU against directing chip supplies. Germany risks recession as the Iran energy shock hits growth.

**Americas:**
A former Pentagon and CIA advisor predicts that President Trump is about to end the U.S. dependence on foreign supply chains for metals. US inflation jumped to 4.2% in May amid a Middle East energy shock, marking the highest since early 2023.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Asia:**
Chinese military jets circled Taiwan as the world's AI supply chain chiefs gathered at Computex. The global Narrow Woven Fabrics Market, valued at USD 3.50 Billion in 2025, projects steady expansion through 2033, fueled by industrial automation across military supply chains.

**Africa:**
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa announced the creation of an “Intelligent Population Register” containing biometric data for every person in South Africa to crack down on illegal immigration.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>
**Asia:**
South Korea's Q1 GDP grew 1.8% quarter-on-quarter, beating advance estimates. Chinese military jets circled Taiwan during Computex.

**Americas:**
California's election problems are reportedly getting worse. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum launched the Universal Health Service on June 1, 2026, to guarantee free, comprehensive medical care for all 130 million citizens. Vertical Data and Ascenty announced a partnership to deploy AI infrastructure across Latin America, bringing hardware procurement, financing, and managed services to Ascenty's 40 data centers in Brazil, Chile, Mexico, and Colombia.

**Europe:**
Neo4j is plotting a Palantir alternative with its GraphAware acquisition, offering an on-prem, air-gapped intel stack to governments. SK Telecom received EU backing for a quantum project. Telefonica Germany partnered with OQ Technology for a D2D LEO satellite trial. Nokia launched automated DDoS protection. The UK is actively addressing its semiconductor rethink.

**Oceania:**
The S&P/NZX 50 Index closed up 1.27% at 13,204.08. Record conflicts are driving peace to a historic low as AI warfare surges.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
Narendra Modi now leads India as its longest-serving elected head of government, drawing comparisons to Jawaharlal Nehru for shaping India's future. Coca-Cola's bottler IPO arrived amidst a shortage of Diet Coke cans, a situation linked to ongoing conflicts in the Middle East tightening the global aluminum supply chain and underscoring India's urgent need to enhance its aluminum industry. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma pitched for deeper investment frameworks and commercial linkages with European markets during a 'Team Europe' delegation visit to Guwahati. Guwahati may also host summit-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, as Assam seeks Japanese investment again. India is looking at coking coal assets and nickel from Russia, having sent a delegation for preliminary talks last month. AGNIT Semiconductors opened a ₹3 crore GaN testing and qualification lab at IISc Bengaluru, aiming for rapid in-house validation, reduced external dependency, enhanced customer confidence, and strengthened market readiness across defense, telecom, and next-generation RF sectors. India's booming local-delivery model enables consumers to buy goods online and receive them within 30 minutes.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
President Donald Trump blamed Iran for downing a U.S. Army Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, stating the United States must respond and vowing retaliation. The crew of the downed helicopter were rescued by an uncrewed drone boat. Israel struck Tyre, Lebanon, killing at least eight people after issuing a first-ever full evacuation order, raising fears among locals that Israel will occupy their homes or expand its invasion in southern Lebanon. Israel's pursuit of security buffer zones is cited as a rational response to military threats, terrorism, and geographic vulnerability. War damage and a blockade have worsened economic conditions for many struggling Iranians. China's May wholesale inflation hit a near four-year high due to Iran war-led higher input costs and the AI boom. Oil prices climbed as US-Iran tensions flared again while stockpiles tightened. A senior Iranian lawmaker indicated regional energy infrastructure could be targeted if the US attacks Iran. Pro-Iran hackers outsmarted a Meta AI Chatbot and accessed high-profile accounts. US stock futures advanced with chipmakers extending their rally, partly due to signs of easing tensions in the Middle East. The Dow Jones surged 389.58 points and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.27% on AI optimism and easing geopolitical tensions. Germany risks recession as the Iran energy shock hits growth. Israel is set to lead the Eastern Mediterranean Gas Forum, signaling a broader energy push. Robo.ai subsidiary Neurovia AI's newly appointed Chief Operating Officer, Rashed Aleghfeli, is participating at the 2026 UAE Data Center Infrastructure & Cloud Summit. The UAE is moving to put AI agents at the center of government. As hiring sentiment weakens, UAE firms are doubling down on AI governance. US inflation jumped to 4.2% in May amid a Middle East energy shock, marking the highest since early 2023. The US energy chief stated unawareness of the US taking oil out of Iran.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The coming weeks will likely see continued high volatility in global energy markets and increased scrutiny on critical mineral supply chains, driven by sustained tensions in West Asia. The US response to Iran's actions will be a primary geopolitical determinant. The ongoing tech competition, particularly in AI and semiconductors, will intensify as Taiwan implements stricter export controls to align with US policy, potentially leading to further fragmentation of global tech supply chains. The drive for domestic semiconductor manufacturing and critical mineral independence in the US and Europe will continue, while emerging AI governance frameworks in regions like the UAE indicate a global pivot towards responsible AI development. Economic indicators, such as inflation and GDP growth, will remain sensitive to geopolitical developments and technological shifts.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
